prompts.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: photorealistic game scene plate, landscape 1536 x 1024.
Primary request: A real photographed nineteenth century antique forged iron safe, viewed dead straight on in a quiet old counting house. This photograph will be split into a hinged door and stationary room so all door edges MUST be perfectly horizontal and vertical. No camera tilt or wide angle distortion.
Subject: one extremely heavy square charcoal-black iron safe cabinet with a thick forged frame, restrained substantial hammered rivets, block feet and overhanging lid lip. A slightly inset rectangular door. Two dark iron combination mechanisms on the LEFT half of the door, one above the other, both with dark engraved rings and a substantial circular knurled black steel knob. Small stationary triangular index at exactly 12 o'clock above each ring. Leave numeral rings UNNUMBERED (precise game numbers will be overlaid later). A large dark iron six-spoked wheel on the RIGHT half of the door, six rounded iron grip knobs on the rim and a substantial center boss. Hinges on the cabinet's RIGHT stile; a small latch on the LEFT stile. No handles elsewhere.
Materials: dark charcoal forged iron, subtle soft mottling, rubbed edge wear, actual shallow scratches and irregular oil stains. Smooth heavy aged iron, never concrete, sand, speckled noise, gold paint, polished bronze, shiny brass or game-engine materials. Sophisticated documentary photograph of a real object, completely believable.
Composition/framing: landscape 3:2 image. The safe is centered at 47% image width. Safe cabinet front occupies approximately x=32% to 63% and y=22% to 81%; keep the entire lid and both feet in frame. Door rectangle approximately x=35% to 61% and y=29% to 76%. The two dial centers at 41% width, 43% and 62% height; wheel center at 53% width 51% height. Enough room on right for the door to swing. The large heavy cabinet is square. Camera lens very long, straight on, close to orthographic; only a little top depth and thin right body side visible.
Scene/backdrop: warm gray old plaster wall, worn wide oak floorboards, faded threadbare red-beige Persian rug beneath safe. Room is spare, NO furniture, no plants, no props, no other objects. Rug visible under all feet. Floor below safe and wall above safe.
Lighting/mood: soft overcast window light from upper left. Exquisitely tactile quiet earthy documentary photography, warm wall and floor against nearly black iron. Even-lit door texture, shadows delicate and realistic.
Constraints: NO typography, titles, branding, label panels, diagrams, watermark, UI, extra safes, decorative gold trim, CGI appearance. CLOSED SAFE ONLY.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: matching photographic game cabinet INTERIOR plate.
Input images: Image 1 is the exact photograph to edit and preserve.
Primary request: Remove ONLY the rectangular front door and its dial and wheel hardware, revealing a dark antique iron safe interior. The entire rest of the photograph must remain identical. The missing door opening is exactly the rectangle from x=476 to x=1040 and y=228 to y=774 on this 1536x1024 photograph.
Inside that same rectangular opening photograph a deep dark charcoal iron cavity, one thick dark iron horizontal shelf at about y=568. Both upper and lower compartments completely EMPTY. Subtle soft window light from the upper left reaches the shelf's front edge and left interior wall. Back wall dark, naturally shadowed metal; plausible depth. There are no drawers, partitions, valuables or internal mechanisms.
Constraints: Keep cabinet frame, lid, rivets, feet, LEFT latch, RIGHT hinges, rug, plaster wall, floor, camera, crop, all colors and lighting absolutely pixel-aligned with the input. Door is completely absent, not anywhere in frame; NO OPEN DOOR ON THE SIDE. No objects, NO gold bars, NO coins. No changes outside the rectangular door opening. The right hinges remain attached to the right frame. Photorealistic heavy black iron with the same authentic material.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: photographic electronic safe door variant.
Input image: edit target, exact closed iron safe photograph.
Primary request: Replace ONLY the TWO CIRCULAR COMBINATION DIALS on the LEFT HALF of the inset door with ONE slender rectangular recessed black steel electronic keypad, running vertically where those two dials were. Keypad housing fits between x=530 and x=698, y=324 and y=670 in this 1536x1024 image. At its top a recessed dark smoked-glass readout approximately x=549..679, y=352..405, with a faint warm red ember interior glow and NO characters. Below it ten physical small rectangular dull black keys in a standard 3x3 grid with a single zero key centered beneath. Mark keys with engraved legible numerals 1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 9 / 0. The keypad is old, worn, believable retrofit electronic equipment on an antique iron safe; restrained dim red-orange electronics, NO neon or sci-fi.
Keep absolutely everything else IDENTICAL: the SIX-spoked IRON WHEEL at the RIGHT, its grip knobs and central boss, the door rectangle and scratches, ALL frame rivets, RIGHT HINGES, LEFT LATCH, lid, feet, rug, plaster, floor, exact camera and lighting. DO NOT enlarge or reposition the safe. Original photo geometry preserved precisely. NO extra dial or knob on left. Photograph only, no text outside keypad, no watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: matching photographic game interior GOLD reward plate.
Input image is the exact doorless open empty iron cabinet photograph to preserve.
Primary request: Add ONE SINGLE small realistic gold bullion bar resting on the existing iron shelf in the upper compartment, near the center-right, approximately x=800 to x=924, y=437 to y=502 in this 1536x1024 photograph. The bar is a heavy squat trapezoidal antique bullion ingot, about the size of a hand, long axis horizontal, warm deep rich gold with subtle rubbed wear, slightly uneven cast edges, faint stamped motif but no readable logo or text. Perspective matches the shelf and camera. The top surface catches the same soft upper-left window light; dark natural shadow directly underneath it. It is an understated rare little find inside the dark safe, not a glowing fantasy treasure.
Keep EVERYTHING else IDENTICAL and pixel-registered to the input: empty lower compartment, shelf shape, all cabinet framing, hinges, latch, lid, feet, wall, floor, rug, camera, lighting. No door, no extra bar, no pile, no coins, no aura, no jewelry. Edit ONLY the small region for this one bar and its shadow.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: matching photographic game interior BRASS reward plate.
Input image is the exact doorless open EMPTY iron cabinet photograph to preserve.
Primary request: Add a small handful of COMMON BRASS COINS resting on the existing iron shelf in the upper compartment, near the center-right, approximately x=760..940, y=445..504 in this 1536x1024 image. One short uneven stack of about seven coins and six loosely scattered coins beside it. Aged subdued yellow-brown brass, visibly round thin stamped currency with rubbed edges, NOT bright gold, NOT bullion bars. Natural believable small objects on a real shelf, illuminated by the exact same soft window light from upper left with subtle grounded shadows.
Keep EVERYTHING else IDENTICAL: completely empty lower compartment, upper back wall, shelf, all frame and body, hinges, latch, lid, feet, wall, floor, rug, camera crop. Edit ONLY the little pile of brass coins and their shadow. No safe door visible, no gold bars, no treasure chest, no extra objects or dramatic glow.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: photo plate for the REVERSE / INTERIOR FACE of a hinged iron safe door.
Input image is the exact closed safe photograph for editing.
Primary request: Within ONLY the inset rectangular door (x=478..1038 and y=230..772 in this 1536x1024 image), REMOVE the two dials, the large wheel, and the two triangular indices, and show instead the INSIDE FACE of this same door as though the door was detached, turned around, and placed flush against the cabinet. Flat dark forged iron back plate, aged and mildly greasy, with a heavy steel horizontal bolt mechanism crossing its midline and a small center hub. Two thick rectangular locking bolts on the LEFT edge. All hardware dark heavy iron, naturally photographed. No ornament, no electronics, no numbers, no dials, no spokes, NO shiny gold or brass. Authentic working antique safe door rear with its utilitarian iron boltwork.
Keep rectangle size, all outside cabinet frame, RIGHT hinges, LEFT latch, feet, lid, wall, rug, floor, camera and light IDENTICAL and pixel-aligned. Dead straight on, no perspective, soft light upper-left matching original, smooth dark charcoal forged iron, not gritty concrete or noise. This will be cropped as a plane for a photographic door opening animation.
